cells.tense: Right now the picturing runs off what has already been lived through.
cells.ask: Take one thing you know you want and name the very next step out loud. Not the whole route, just the one step. Then do it before the day ends.
cells.core:
What you picture ahead isn't fantasy and it isn't a plan you're holding over your own head. You've been through enough that the next step tends to show up, and you take it without needing the whole road mapped first. The picturing here is built out of what already happened to you, and it holds up under weight.

The weight you carry hasn't made you rigid and it hasn't made you quit. You bear what's in front of you and still let something in you lean toward what's coming. The one thing to watch: this kind of ease is quiet, so it's easy to stop choosing. Ask what the next step is and take it. The momentum you feel will look after itself.

cells.tense: You are already living inside a picture that the day hasn't agreed to yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing still in the future and let it stay there this week. Don't build it, don't fix it, don't carry it. When it comes up, put it down and choose one small thing that's actually here.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead of you is a version of this that finally makes sense, and you're carrying it around all day. You rehearse it, you add to it, you plan who you'll be when it arrives. Meanwhile the load in your hands gets borne by somebody who's half somewhere else, and the strength you're spending goes to a future that keeps moving.

The picture and the day have swapped jobs. It stops when you can let tomorrow stay unbuilt and still hold what's real. Care for what's growing means leaving it room to grow by itself, without you leaning on it. Let the future be somebody else's for a week. What's under your feet is enough to stand on.

cells.tense: You want the whole road before you take one step on a road you can't see the end of.
cells.ask: Say the one thing you want before you can say why. One sentence, out loud, to no one in front of you. Then write what you notice and do not explain it yet.
cells.core:
You want the whole road handed to you before you'll take a single step on a road you can't see the end of. So the load gets carried and the leaning stops. Nothing here is a mystery to you, and that's the point. The bearing still works. Trusting the path to reveal itself doesn't.

Pushing harder into holding won't fill what's thin here. What's thin is the part of you that knows what matters before it knows why. That part gets fed by one honest sentence about what you want, said before you can justify it. You don't have to follow it anywhere tonight. You just have to let it be said, and let what you notice be enough.

cells.tense: The picturing is already shaping what you carry, and you call it just getting on with it.
cells.ask: Pick one of the lines you say about your life and write it on paper before you next speak it out loud. When you speak it, say plainly where it came from.
cells.core:
The picture you hold of how this goes is steering plenty — what you take on, what you turn down, how long you keep holding. You talk about it like it's just how things are. Something is doing the steering and it isn't being owned.

A small repeated practice is the way in. Write down one of the lines you keep saying — about what's possible, about what you can stand — and look at it as yours. Something that happens once a day and takes minutes is enough; the point is attention, not effort. You'll find the line harder to see than to say. That's not the failing. That's the entry. Say where it came from.
